title: 観世流謡本 (Kanze-ryū Utaibon), Vol. 11a
shelf_note: A Kanze utaibon in cursive print, with chant notation (goma-ten) and red-ink performance marks. It belongs on a Japanese/Noh shelf. Plays seen: Tsunemasa (p.26), Kochō (p.49), Torioibune (p.64).
structure_note: There are 152 page records against a pages_count of 102, and 144 translated pages against a pages_translated of 96, so the book-level counters are stale. The 2 printed backsteps are most likely misread numbers, not a real ordering defect: the OCR turns rows of chant-notation dots into digit strings (e.g. 'ハ一一二一一八一二十一人'), so printed-number detection is unreliable on this book.

book_verdict: The NDL-koten transcriptions are mostly the right text, apart from notation noise, one invented date and stray numeral strings. The English is unreliable on all four pages, and on two of them it is not a translation of the page at all.
reader_summary: A Kanze school chant book in cursive print with chant notation, holding several plays (Tsunemasa, Kochō, Torioibune). The Japanese transcription is broadly the right text, but chant marks are read as numbers, and in one place as a date. The English cannot be trusted: on every sampled page it drops content or invents it.

title: 観世流謡本 (Kanze-ryū Utaibon), Vol. 3
shelf_note: A Kanze utaibon in cursive print. Plays seen: Yorimasa (pp.25, 40), Hachi no ki (p.79), Hagoromo (p.101).
structure_note: There are 167 page records against a pages_count of 112, and 152 translated pages against a pages_translated of 108, so the counters are stale. The 4 backsteps and 4 repeats most likely come from the 'dates' the OCR invents from margin titles ('十一月廿一日', '十一月十一日'), taken as printed page numbers. They are not a real ordering defect.

book_verdict: The transcription is good for a cursive utaibon: minor misreads, plus 'dates' invented from margin titles. The English misses the dramatic point of every sampled page and misnames Byōdō-in.
reader_summary: A Kanze school chant book holding Yorimasa, Hachi no ki and Hagoromo. The Japanese transcription is the right text, with small misreads and spurious date headings. The English is not usable as a translation: on every sampled page key lines are dropped or invented.

title: 観世流改訂謡本 (Kanze-ryū Noh Texts)
shelf_note: A 1912 revised Kanze utaibon of the play Tamura; all four sampled pages are from Tamura. The generic title hides that this volume holds a single play. Attributing Tamura to Zeami is the conventional attribution.
structure_note: 28 records and the counts are consistent. Page 3 is the play's first page, and a University of Illinois library due-date slip pasted over its centre hides most of the opening text. The single backstep is most likely a misread folio numeral.

book_verdict: A 1912 Kanze utaibon of a single play (Tamura) under a generic title. The Gemini OCR confabulates lines in the kuse (p.15) and wraps notation into <gloss> tags, and the English follows those errors.
reader_summary: This is the Noh play Tamura in a 1912 Kanze edition, not a general collection of Noh texts. On some pages the transcription is roughly the right text, but it invents whole lines in the dance section and fills the text with notation tags. The English follows those errors, so passages read fluently but do not say what the page says.

title: Genji Monogatari Ekotoba (源氏物語絵詞), Vol. 1
shelf_note: An illustrated Genji handscroll from the National Diet Library (photo label: 『源氏物語絵巻』 請求記号 ん-98). The text sections seen come from the Uji chapters (Yadorigi, Azumaya).
structure_note: 'published: 1100' is wrong for this object. It is a later painted copy of the Heian Genji scroll, held by the NDL under call number ん-98, with accession stamps dated Meiji 44 and Taishō 1. The scan label titles it 源氏物語絵巻, not 絵詞. Page counts are consistent (19).

book_verdict: The NDL scans of this illustrated Genji scroll copy are fine and the kana transcription is mostly sound. The English is invented on all four pages, including a note that dismisses the text as generic tropes, and the date '1100' misdescribes a later copy.
reader_summary: A later painted copy of the illustrated Tale of Genji scroll, held by the National Diet Library, with text sections from the Uji chapters (Yadorigi, Azumaya). On the text-heavy pages the kana transcription is close to the scroll. The English is not a translation: it invents content on every sampled page and leaves out the waka.
